landmarks.name: Asmara
landmarks.writeup: The capital city known for its well-preserved Italian colonial modernist architecture, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

landmarks.name: Massawa
landmarks.writeup: A historic port city on the Red Sea with Ottoman and Italian architectural influences.

landmarks.name: Dahlak Archipelago
landmarks.writeup: A group of islands in the Red Sea famous for marine biodiversity and diving spots.

landmarks.name: Keren
landmarks.writeup: The second-largest city, known for its vibrant markets and nearby historical battle sites.

landmarks.name: Nakfa
landmarks.writeup: A town symbolic for its role in the Eritrean War of Independence.

cultural_events.name: Independence Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on May 24th, marking Eritrea's independence from Ethiopia in 1993.

cultural_events.name: Meskel
cultural_events.writeup: An important religious festival celebrated by Eritrean Orthodox Christians commemorating the discovery of the True Cross.

cultural_events.name: Eid al-Fitr
cultural_events.writeup: A significant Islamic holiday marking the end of Ramadan, celebrated by Eritrea's Muslim population.

food_writeup: Eritrean cuisine features injera (a sourdough flatbread) served with spicy stews called tsebhi, often made with meat, lentils, or vegetables, reflecting a blend of African and Middle Eastern culinary traditions.
brief_history: Eritrea was an Italian colony from the late 19th century until World War II, then administered by Britain before being federated with Ethiopia in 1952. After a 30-year war of independence, Eritrea gained sovereignty in 1993. The country has since faced political challenges and conflicts, including a border war with Ethiopia.

important_people.name: Isaias Afwerki
important_people.description: First and current President of Eritrea

important_people.name: Hamid Idris Awate
important_people.description: Leader of the Eritrean armed struggle for independence

current_conflicts: Tense relations and occasional border disputes with Ethiopia persist despite a 2018 peace agreement; internal political repression and human rights concerns are also reported.
